programme.title: Atlantic: The Wildest Ocean on Earth
programme.desc: Documentary examining the animals pitting themselves against the world's wildest ocean, unveiling the natural forces that underpin life in the Atlantic. In the vast South Atlantic, huge pods of dolphins, massive penguin colonies and the largest gathering of marine mammals on Earth pack chains of extraordinary islands, created by powerful volcanic forces far below them. Meanwhile, the nutrient-rich upwellings create profusions of life in some areas, and the abyssal depths host a world of bizarre creatures in others

programme.title: A Slow Odyssey
programme.desc: An immersive journey into the world of a green sea turtle, using only natural sounds and embedded graphics to deliver detailed information about its daily routine

programme.title: Timeshift
programme.desc: Antiques Roadshow's Paul Atterbury recalls the heyday of the great ocean liners, travelling round Britain to reveal a story of design, politics and tragedy as he finds out how these great ships captured the public's imagination. Along the way he uncovers a cinema in Scotland built from the interiors of the SS Homeric, and visits a house in Poole, Dorset, where cabins from the Mauretania have been preserved

programme.title: Atlantic: The Wildest Ocean on Earth
programme.desc: Documentary examining the animals pitting themselves against the world's wildest ocean, unveiling the natural forces that underpin life in the Atlantic. programme.title: Treasures of Ancient Greece
programme.desc: Alastair Sooke traces the complex and fascinating story of Western civilisation's love affair with Greek art, learning how people in succeeding centuries found inspiration for their own ideals and ambitions. Filming in Britain, France, Italy and Germany, Alastair visits the Aphrodite of Knidos, which was the first naked woman in Western art; the bronze horses of St Mark's in Venice, which became a pawn in an imperial game; and the Discobolus, which was purchased by Nazi leader Adolf Hitler

programme.title: Egypt's Lost Cities
programme.desc: Dallas Campbell and Liz Bonnin join Dr Sarah Parcak on a journey to Egypt to find out whether cities, temples and pyramids are lying beneath the sands. The potential existence of the buildings was suggested by satellites as part of an alternative approach to archaeology

programme.title: Becoming Frida Kahlo
programme.desc: The documentary charts Frida's time in San Francisco with Diego Riera, where her style caused great excitement and she became determined to succeed in her own right. Later, she became shocked by the vast gap between rich and poor that she witnessed in Depression-era New York, and struggled to hide her disdain for high society

programme.title: Leonardo
programme.sub-title: The Secret Life of the Mona Lisa
programme.desc: Alan Yentob tells the story of how Leonardo Da Vinci's Mona Lisa became the most famous painting in the world. Admired by six million tourists every year, surrounded by bodyguards and encased in a humidified, air-conditioned box protected by bullet-proof glass, the enigmatic masterpiece has been stolen, vandalised and exploited over the centuries. With the help of leading scholars and original research, the subject of the portrait is finally revealed - along with the reason behind her inscrutable smile

programme.title: Corridors of Power: Should America Police the World?
programme.sub-title: Libya - If You Break It You Own It
programme.desc: A look at Barack Obama's first presidential trip abroad to Cairo, where he addressed the younger generation in the Arab world and told them 'you, more than anyone, have the ability to remake this world'. A year and a half later the Arab Spring broke out, leaving Obama to decide whether he should heed the call to save innocent civilians from Muammar Gaddafi's threats of a potential massacre

programme.title: Great British Railway Journeys
programme.sub-title: Dundee to Loch of the Lowes
programme.desc: Michael Portillo's rail journey through post-war Scotland takes him over the River Tay to Dundee, Scotland's fourth largest city. He is on the trail of Joseph McKenzie, the father of modern Scottish photography. Alighting at Dunkeld, the host makes for the Loch of the Lowes, to spot a pair of breeding ospreys

programme.title: Walking with
programme.desc: Chef Monica Galetti ventures through the landscapes of the North York Moors, along the way she meets local residents and samples local produce. Monica begins in the historic village of Rosedale Abey, before following the course of a stream up Rosedale and climbing towards the heather. Crossing over to Farndale, she walks the quiet lanes and ends with a drink in the hamlet of Church Houses

programme.title: Keeping Up Appearances
programme.desc: Hyacinth develops a passion for art, Rose acquires a new admirer, and Daddy has a yearning to join the Foreign Legion. Patricia Routledge stars

programme.title: One Foot in the Grave
programme.desc: Victor endures a sleepless night - and naturally ensures the eternally put-upon Margaret and their neighbours share in his suffering. Comedy, starring Richard Wilson and Annette Crosbie

programme.title: She-Wolves: England's Early Queens
programme.desc: Historian Helen Castor explores the lives of Isabella of France and Margaret of Anjou, two French-born queens of England whose ambition and desire for power caused outrage in medieval Britain. Isabella, wife of King Edward II in the 14th century, was accused of murder, while 100 years later Margaret, who was married to Henry VI, was regarded as a destructively ambitious figure - and would go on to be labelled a 'she-wolf' by Shakespeare. However, Castor argues it was their gender, rather than their behaviour, that lay at the root of their public vilification

programme.title: Castles: Britain's Fortified History
programme.desc: Historian Sam Willis charts how Edward I turned the castle into an instrument of colonisation. He spent a large amount of money on subduing the Welsh and built fearsome fortresses in Caernarfon, Gwynedd and Beaumaris, which were used to impose England's rule on the country. However, when the king's attention turned to Scotland, his plans didn't go as expected

programme.title: Corridors of Power: Should America Police the World?
programme.sub-title: Darfur - Carrots for a War Criminal
programme.desc: A look at how, in 2003, the Sudanese government began a widespread ethnic cleansing campaign in the western part of the country. Hundreds of thousands of Americans went out to protest and demand protection for the citizens of Darfur. Following Obama's 2008 election success, many of the people that fought so vocally for Darfur came into office

programme.title: The Treasures of Ancient Rome
programme.desc: Alastair Sooke explores the artistic achievements of the Romans, tracing their progression from thieves and copycats to pioneers of the use of unflinching realism. Portraits from the Republic reveal how they captured lifelike images and immortalised figures such as Julius Caesar and Cicero using marble, bronze and paint. Alastair also looks at how Rome's first emperor, Augustus, used art as a tool to forge his dominion

programme.title: Heir Hunters

programme.title: Four in a Bed

programme.title: Four in a Bed

programme.title: Come Dine with Me

programme.title: Come Dine with Me
programme.desc: Australian admin assistant Kimberley Thomas hosts the fourth dinner party in Cheltenham and hopes that an evening of sophistication will win her the £1,000 prize. programme.desc: Abby Norton welcomes her fellow hoteliers to Newchester Farmhouse B&B in Merriott, Somerset. Collette and Danny are impressed by the superstar quality beds, although Justin and Mike find the linen lacking - and Keith just misses modern technology

programme.title: Four in a Bed

programme.desc: The B&Bers meet for the last time to find out how much they've been paid and to settle some scores. programme.title: Location, Location, Location
programme.desc: Kirstie Allsopp and Phil Spencer search for properties in west London. Philip is with Jody and Shane, originally from Canada and Australia. For these foodies it's all about cooking and entertaining space. Can Kirstie find them a house with all the right ingredients?

programme.title: Grand Designs

The couple want to transform a 1960s forester's lodge into a unique Japanese house, complete with a tatami room - decorated in her homeland's traditional style - sliding paper walls and a bath on the roof. Keen to keep costs down, they have decided to engage only the design skills - rather than the full services - of an architect, so with no previous building experience they tackle the project alone

programme.title: Oti and Richard's South African Odyssey
programme.desc: Oti and Richard explore the province of KwaZulu-Natal and the beach city of Durban. At the famous Victoria Street Market, they taste Durban's signature dish: bunny chow. In Pietermaritzburg, they learn about the life of young Mahatma Gandhi and meet his granddaughter Ela. Along the Dolphin Coast, they explore Zulu culture, and meet a healer who says they have a message from Oti's late grandmother

programme.title: 24 Hours in A&E
programme.desc: On a busy Saturday night at King's College Hospital, staff have to juggle the needs of elderly patients and sick children alongside those who are drunk or violent. programme.title: 24 Hours in Police Custody

programme.title: 24 Hours in A&E

programme.title: A Place in the Sun
programme.desc: Tracey and Dean met in their early twenties and have devoted their lives to raising their family, including their own three children and two foster children. programme.title: Heir Hunters

programme.title: Four in a Bed
programme.desc: Day four is at the Foxhunter Park in Kent, where brother and sister Jane Stacey and Russell Saunders own a caravan site that includes a bistro and entertainment. programme.title: Four in a Bed

programme.title: Cover Your Ears (2023)

programme.title: David Attenborough's Natural Curiosities
programme.desc: The naturalist continues to explore the secrets behind evolution, this time focusing on the animal kingdom's bizarre hybrids, including the 'pizzly bear', a cross between a polar bear and a grizzly, which is thought to have come into being as a result of global warming. He also covers the killer bee brought into existence due to the transfer of African bees to South America

programme.title: David Attenborough's Natural Curiosities
programme.desc: Footage of animals that have unusual means of finding their way around. Dung beetles are able to navigate by the sky, using the position of the sun, moon and stars to determine which is the right direction to go in, while pigeons display remarkable powers of memory, able to recall complex travel routes and follow manmade roads and hedgerows

programme.title: David Attenborough's Natural Curiosities
programme.desc: The naturalist explores the extremes of birth in the animal kingdom, explaining why the giant panda gives birth to the smallest babies of any existing mammal. He also looks at the kiwi, asking why the bird produces a single egg that is a quarter of its body mass - one of the largest in the world - and almost too big to lay

programme.title: David Attenborough's Natural Curiosities
programme.desc: The naturalist investigates whether animals and plants have developed an awareness of mathematics, including bamboos that flower exactly the same around the world. Plus, the story of a German horse named Hans that was declared a mathematical genius, but all was not as it seemed

programme.title: David Attenborough's Natural Curiosities
programme.desc: The veteran naturalist investigates two shells that have proved to be winners in evolution - the bird's egg shell and the hard shell of the tortoise. The ostrich egg is so strong it is possible for it to take a person's weight without breaking - so how does a chick manage break out of such a fortress? The evolution of the tortoise shell was for a long time a mystery, and this bony box offers a lot more than just protection

programme.title: David Attenborough's Natural Curiosities
programme.desc: The evolutionary documentary concludes, as David Attenborough profiles the Siamese fighting fish, so aggressive it will fight its own reflection until it is exhausted. He also looks at the kangaroo - once pitted against humans in the boxing ring - which has a kick so strong it can kill

However, the family home is no longer suitable for Amanda - so that's where Nick Knowles and the rest of the DIY SOS team come in, strengthened by a number of local tradesmen

programme.title: Tipping Point
programme.desc: Ben Shephard hosts the quiz in which contestants answer questions to win turns on an arcade-style machine. Dropping tokens down a choice of four chutes, they hope to knock piles of them off a moving shelf - and the more they collect, the greater the prize fund. The player who has won the least amount is then eliminated, and the last one standing competes for a £10,000 jackpot
